method: Lean .ilean v5 resolved constant usages; owner-module filtering; unique symbol/source spans; public-manifest/index and exact source-token checks.
limitations: One use means one distinct compiler-recorded constant/name/source-span reference, not a runtime call.
Counted references appear in definitions, theorem statements, proof scripts, section variables and checked examples.
Implementation modules include inline anonymous examples and named regression fixtures; they are not exclusively production proofs.
No comment mentions, import lines, scratch files, generated copies, dependency-internal uses or transitive uses are counted.
Implicit elaborator/tactic/simp dependencies without a corresponding source-name reference are not counted.
The same declaration may occur in several categories; distinct category counts must not be added.
Owned PMF additions are credited to LeanInfoTheory; mathlib-owned PMF declarations are excluded.
Repeated references are sensitive to notation, proof style and refactoring. Counts do not measure code, time or effort saved.
Declarations may be mathematically important even when explicitly referenced only once.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsCondIndependentOf
declarations.documentation: Two random variables are conditionally independent given a third when their mapped triple law is conditionally independent.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsIndependent
declarations.documentation: A joint PMF is independent when it is the product of its marginals.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsIndependentOf
declarations.documentation: Two random variables are independent when their joint law is independent.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsMarkovChain
declarations.documentation: A triple PMF is a Markov chain in its first-to-second-to-third coordinate order.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsMarkovChainOf
declarations.documentation: Random variables `X`, `Y`, and `Z` form the Markov chain `X → Y → Z` when `X` and `Z` are conditionally independent given `Y`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.apply_eq_zero_of_fstMarginal_eq_zero
declarations.documentation: If a first marginal atom has zero mass, then every joint atom over that first coordinate has zero mass.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.apply_eq_zero_of_sndMarginal_eq_zero
declarations.documentation: If a second marginal atom has zero mass, then every joint atom over that second coordinate has zero mass.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.apply_le_fstMarginal
declarations.documentation: A joint atom mass is bounded by the mass of its first marginal atom. This is the basic support/domination fact behind conditioning on the first coordinate.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.apply_le_sndMarginal
declarations.documentation: A joint atom mass is bounded by the mass of its second marginal atom.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelJoint_condFstGivenSndChannel
declarations.documentation: Sampling the total conditional channel from the second marginal reconstructs the original pair law with its coordinates in channel input-output order.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy
declarations.documentation: Conditional entropy `H(alpha | beta)` of a finite joint PMF on `alpha × beta`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyFstGivenSnd
declarations.documentation: Entropy of the conditional fiber, with explicit zero-mass branch. This helper is intended for expected conditional entropy formulas. If `P_B(b)=0`, the branch is the number `0`, not the entropy of an arbitrary default conditional PMF.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyFstGivenSnd_of_sndMarginal_ne_zero
declarations.documentation: On nonzero conditioning atoms, `condEntropyFstGivenSnd` is the entropy of the canonical conditional PMF `P_{A | B=b}`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf
declarations.documentation: Conditional entropy `H(X | Y)` for finite-valued random variables.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_eq
declarations.documentation: Random-variable conditional entropy rewrites to joint entropy minus entropy of the conditioning variable.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_eq_zero_iff_exists_function
declarations.documentation: Conditional entropy of finite-valued random variables is zero exactly when the first variable is a function of the second on the source PMF support.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_eq_sum_sndMarginal_mul_condEntropyFstGivenSnd
declarations.documentation: Expected conditional entropy formula for the finite conditional-law API: `H(A | B) = sum_b p_B(b) * H(P_{A | B=b})`. The right-hand side is written using `condEntropyFstGivenSnd`, whose value is `0` on zero-marginal conditioning atoms and the entropy of the canonical conditional PMF on nonzero atoms.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd
declarations.documentation: Conditional law of the first coordinate given a nonzero second-coordinate atom. Mathematically, this is the finite PMF `P_{A | B=b}(a) = P_{A,B}(a,b) / P_B(b)`. The proof argument `hb : sndMarginal p b ≠ 0` is part of the API so that zero-probability conditioning atoms do not receive a fake default distribution.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSndChannel
declarations.documentation: The total channel from the second coordinate to the first associated with a joint PMF. For `P_B(b) != 0`, this is the canonical conditional law `P_{A | B=b}`. For a null fiber, it is the first marginal `P_A`. The fallback supplies a PMF without requiring an additional `Nonempty alpha` assumption; it has no intended conditional semantics and disappears from the weighted reconstruction laws.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSndChannel_of_sndMarginal_eq_zero
declarations.documentation: On a null conditioning fiber, the total channel uses the documented fallback.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSndChannel_of_sndMarginal_ne_zero
declarations.documentation: On a positive conditioning fiber, the total channel is the canonical conditional PMF.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condFstGivenSnd_apply
declarations.documentation: Atom formula for the conditional law: `P_{A | B=b}(a) = P_{A,B}(a,b) / P_B(b)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf
declarations.documentation: Conditional mutual information `I(X; Y | Z)` for finite-valued random variables.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf_eq_condEntropyOf_sub_condEntropyOf
declarations.documentation: Conditional mutual information as a difference of conditional entropies: `I(X;Y|Z) = H(X|Z) - H(X|Y,Z)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf_eq_zero_iff_isMarkovChainOf
declarations.documentation: The Markov condition `X → Y → Z` is equivalent to the textbook zero-CMI identity `I(X;Z | Y) = 0`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf_nonneg
declarations.documentation: Conditional mutual information of finite-valued random variables is nonnegative.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf_swap
declarations.documentation: Conditional mutual information of finite-valued random variables is symmetric in the first two variables: `I(Y;X | Z) = I(X;Y | Z)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbability
declarations.documentation: The probability that a deterministic decoder fails under a joint law. The PMF is a joint law of a source symbol and an observation, in that order.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbability_eq_sum
declarations.documentation: The decoding-error probability is the total mass of the joint atoms on which the decoder fails. This is the main finite-sum elimination theorem for decoding error.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbability_le_one
declarations.documentation: A decoding-error probability is at most one.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.decodingErrorProbability_nonneg
declarations.documentation: A decoding-error probability is nonnegative.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy
declarations.documentation: Shannon entropy, in nats, of a finite probability mass function.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf
declarations.documentation: Entropy of a finite-valued random variable under a discrete law.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_comp_equiv
declarations.documentation: Relabeling a finite-valued random variable by an equivalence preserves its entropy.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyOf_comp_injective
declarations.documentation: Applying an injective relabeling to a finite-valued random variable preserves its entropy.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_map_equiv
declarations.documentation: Entropy is invariant under relabeling the alphabet by an equivalence. This is one of the basic sanity checks for finite entropy: only the masses matter, not the names of the atoms.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_map_injective
declarations.documentation: Entropy is invariant under injective relabeling into a larger finite alphabet. Atoms outside the image of the relabeling have zero pushed-forward mass.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_nonneg
declarations.documentation: Shannon entropy is nonnegative for finite PMFs.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropy_pure
declarations.documentation: A deterministic finite PMF has entropy zero.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal
declarations.documentation: The first marginal of a finite joint PMF.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_apply
declarations.documentation: The mass of the first marginal is the sum of the joint masses over the second coordinate.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_indepProd
declarations.documentation: The first marginal of an independent product is the first factor law.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_map
declarations.documentation: Taking the first marginal after pushing a PMF forward to a pair is the same as pushing forward by the first coordinate of that pair-valued map.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_map_pair
declarations.documentation: For a joint law built from random variables `(X, Y)`, the first marginal is the law of `X`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_map_swap
declarations.documentation: Swapping the two coordinates turns the first marginal into the original second marginal.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstMarginal_ne_zero_of_apply_ne_zero
declarations.documentation: Nonzero joint mass forces the corresponding first marginal mass to be nonzero.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstSndMarginal
declarations.documentation: The marginal on the first and second coordinates of a finite triple PMF.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstSndMarginal_map_triple
declarations.documentation: For a joint law built from `(X, Y, Z)`, the first-second marginal is the joint law of `(X, Y)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstThirdMarginal
declarations.documentation: The marginal on the first and third coordinates of a finite triple PMF.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.fstThirdMarginal_map_triple
declarations.documentation: For a joint law built from `(X, Y, Z)`, the first-third marginal is the joint law of `(X, Z)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.indepProd
declarations.documentation: Independent product of two probability mass functions. Mathematically, this is the law of `(X, Y)` when `X` has law `p`, `Y` has law `q`, and the two variables are independent.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.indepProd_apply
declarations.documentation: The atom mass of an independent product is the product of the two atom masses.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isIndependentOf_iff_map_eq_indepProd
declarations.documentation: Random-variable independence is equality of the joint law with the independent product of the two individual laws.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isIndependentOf_swap
declarations.documentation: Independence of random variables is symmetric.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isIndependent_indepProd
declarations.documentation: The independent product of two PMFs is independent.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isMarkovChainOf_comp
declarations.documentation: Deterministic post-processing of the middle variable always gives the forward Markov chain `X → Y → f(Y)`. Equivalently, `X` and `f(Y)` are conditionally independent given `Y`: `X ⟂ f(Y) | Y`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isMarkovChain_channelExtension
declarations.documentation: Extending any pair law of `(A,B)` by sampling `C` from a channel depending only on `B` produces the Markov chain `A → B → C`. The result is type-generic and includes null middle-coordinate fibers through the cross-product characterization, without requiring a conditional PMF.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isMarkovChain_iff_crossProduct
declarations.documentation: A triple law is Markov in coordinate order exactly when every atom satisfies the cross-product factorization `p(a,b,c) * p_B(b) = p_AB(a,b) * p_BC(b,c)`. The identity also covers null middle-coordinate fibers, so it requires no finite-alphabet or measurable-space assumptions.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isMarkovChain_iff_exists_channelExtension
declarations.documentation: Textbook channel-factorization characterization of a finite Markov triple: a law is Markov exactly when some channel from the middle alphabet extends its first-two marginal to the original triple law.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf
declarations.documentation: Joint entropy of two finite-valued random variables under a discrete law.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo
declarations.documentation: Mutual information `I(alpha; beta)` of a finite joint PMF on `alpha × beta`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf
declarations.documentation: Mutual information `I(X; Y)` for finite-valued random variables.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_chain_rule_fst
declarations.documentation: Random-variable form of `mutualInfo_chain_rule_fst`: `I(X;Y,Z) = I(X;Z) + I(X;Y | Z)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_chain_rule_snd
declarations.documentation: Random-variable form of `mutualInfo_chain_rule_snd`: `I(X;Y,Z) = I(X;Y) + I(X;Z | Y)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_comp_right_le
declarations.documentation: Deterministic post-processing of the right variable cannot increase mutual information.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_eq
declarations.documentation: Random-variable mutual information rewrites to the standard entropy identity `H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_eq_entropyOf_sub_condEntropyOf
declarations.documentation: Random-variable form `I(X;Y) = H(X) - H(X|Y)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_eq_entropyOf_sub_condEntropyOf_swap
declarations.documentation: Symmetric random-variable form `I(X;Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_eq_zero_iff_isIndependentOf
declarations.documentation: Finite-valued random variables have zero mutual information exactly when their mapped joint law is independent.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_le_entropyOf_left
declarations.documentation: Random-variable mutual information is at most `H(X)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_swap
declarations.documentation: Mutual information of finite-valued random variables is symmetric: `I(Y;X) = I(X;Y)`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_eq
declarations.documentation: Unfolding lemma for the entropy-identity definition of mutual information.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_eq_zero_iff_isIndependent
declarations.documentation: Finite mutual information is zero exactly when the joint PMF is independent. The proof chooses the discrete measurable structure only locally, uses the KL representation of mutual information, and discharges the necessary real-KL finiteness guard through support inclusion.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal
declarations.documentation: The second marginal of a finite joint PMF.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_apply
declarations.documentation: The mass of the second marginal is the sum of the joint masses over the first coordinate.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_indepProd
declarations.documentation: The second marginal of an independent product is the second factor law.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_map
declarations.documentation: Taking the second marginal after pushing a PMF forward to a pair is the same as pushing forward by the second coordinate of that pair-valued map.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_map_pair
declarations.documentation: For a joint law built from random variables `(X, Y)`, the second marginal is the law of `Y`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_map_swap
declarations.documentation: Swapping the two coordinates turns the second marginal into the original first marginal.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_ne_zero_of_apply_ne_zero
declarations.documentation: Nonzero joint mass forces the corresponding second marginal mass to be nonzero.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndMarginal_sndThirdMarginal
declarations.documentation: The second marginal of the `(B,C)` law is the law of `C`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sndThirdMarginal
declarations.documentation: The marginal on the second and third coordinates of a finite triple PMF.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.support_condFstGivenSnd
declarations.documentation: The support of `P_{A | B=b}` is the fiber of the joint support over `b`.

declarations.name: LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.thirdMarginal
declarations.documentation: The marginal on the third coordinate of a finite triple PMF.

declarations.name: PMF.binaryMixture
declarations.documentation: The binary mixture with weight `t` on `p` and weight `1 - t` on `q`. Equivalently, a Bernoulli selector chooses `p` on `true` and `q` on `false`.

declarations.name: PMF.binaryMixture_apply
declarations.documentation: Pointwise mass formula for a binary PMF mixture.

declarations.name: PMF.bind_toReal_apply
declarations.documentation: On a finite selector type, the real mass of a bind is the corresponding finite weighted sum of real masses.

declarations.name: PMF.channelExtension
declarations.documentation: Extend a joint law of `(A,B)` by sampling `C` from a channel depending only on `B`. The result uses Lean's right-associated triple type `(A, B, C)`.

declarations.name: PMF.channelExtension_deterministicChannel
declarations.documentation: Extending a pair law through a deterministic channel is its graph pushforward.

declarations.name: PMF.channelJoint
declarations.documentation: The joint law of an input distributed as `p` and an output sampled from `W`.

declarations.name: PMF.channelJoint_apply
declarations.documentation: The induced joint mass factors as input mass times channel mass.

declarations.name: PMF.channelJoint_eq_iff_eq_on_support
declarations.documentation: Two channels induce the same joint law from an input PMF exactly when they agree on every supported input atom. Their values away from the input support are irrelevant.

declarations.name: PMF.channelJoint_map_fst
declarations.documentation: The first projection of an induced joint law is its input law.

declarations.name: PMF.channelJoint_map_snd
declarations.documentation: The second projection of an induced joint law is the channel output law.

declarations.name: PMF.deterministicChannel
declarations.documentation: The deterministic channel induced by a function.

declarations.name: PMF.eq_pure_iff_support_eq_singleton
declarations.documentation: A PMF is pure at `a` exactly when its support is the singleton `{a}`.

declarations.name: PMF.map_apply_eq_zero_of_notMem_range
declarations.documentation: If a target atom is outside the range of a map, then the pushed-forward PMF assigns zero mass to that atom.

declarations.name: PMF.map_apply_equiv
declarations.documentation: Pushing a PMF forward along an equivalence preserves the mass of each atom at the renamed atom.

declarations.name: PMF.map_apply_of_injective
declarations.documentation: If `f` is injective, pushing a PMF forward along `f` preserves the mass of each source atom at its image.

declarations.name: PMF.mem_supportFinset
declarations.documentation: Membership in `p.supportFinset` is membership in the set-valued PMF support.

declarations.name: PMF.mem_support_channelJoint_iff
declarations.documentation: A pair is supported by the induced joint law exactly when both stages support it.

declarations.name: PMF.sum_toReal
declarations.documentation: On a finite type, the real masses of a `PMF` sum to one.

declarations.name: PMF.supportFinset
declarations.documentation: The finite set of atoms to which a finite PMF assigns nonzero mass. Its coercion to a set is `p.support`; this finset view is intended for finite sums and support-cardinality arguments.

declarations.name: PMF.toReal_le_one
declarations.documentation: Each atom of a `PMF` has real mass at most one.

declarations.name: PMF.toReal_nonneg
declarations.documentation: Each atom of a `PMF` has nonnegative real mass.
